description: My laptop screen is completely black and won't turn on, even after holding the power button.
reasoning: A dead device blocks all work with no stated alternative, but it's one person's machine, not an outage -- High, not Critical.

description: I can't install the new version of Photoshop, I keep getting error code 0x80070005.
reasoning: Work is affected but the previous version presumably still runs -- an alternative exists.

description: The office WiFi keeps disconnecting every few minutes, it's happening to me all morning.
reasoning: Disruptive but intermittent, and wired/mobile data is a plausible fallback -- not a full outage.

description: I forgot my password and can't log into my email account at all.
reasoning: Total lockout from a core system, no alternative -- but self-service reset exists and it's one account, not Critical.

description: My mouse cursor is frozen and not moving at all.
reasoning: Annoying but the laptop's own touchpad or keyboard navigation is a working alternative in most cases.

description: Excel keeps crashing whenever I try to open a specific shared spreadsheet.
reasoning: One file/app is affected; other spreadsheet tools or a colleague's copy are reasonable alternatives.

description: I can't connect to the VPN from home, it just times out every time I try.
reasoning: Blocks remote access entirely for this person with no stated alternative -- important work cannot continue.

description: The printer on the 3rd floor is out of toner.
reasoning: Minor, and other printers on campus are an obvious alternative.

description: Could I get a second monitor for my desk? Not urgent, just would help productivity.
reasoning: Explicitly a nice-to-have request, not a problem blocking anything.

description: Our team's shared drive access was revoked overnight and we can't retrieve the files for tomorrow's funding deadline.
reasoning: Blocks a team from critical work with a hard deadline and no alternative -- High under the agreed criteria, since it's not a system-wide outage or a safety/security incident.

description: Zoom freezes every time I try to share my screen during client meetings.
reasoning: Disruptive but another conferencing tool (Teams, Meet) is a workable alternative.

description: A student forwarded us an email asking them to confirm their password through a link -- looks like phishing.
reasoning: A live phishing attempt is a security incident under the agreed criteria, regardless of how many people are affected so far.

description: The projector bulb in Lecture Hall 2 just burned out and class starts in ten minutes.
reasoning: Urgent and blocks the class, but a single room's equipment failure isn't a major outage or safety/security issue -- High, not Critical.

description: The entire building lost network connectivity about five minutes ago -- no one can get online.
reasoning: A building-wide outage is exactly the 'major outage' case the Critical tier describes.

description: My OneDrive hasn't synced in three days and I'm worried about losing recent changes.
reasoning: A real risk but not yet a confirmed loss, and local copies still work in the meantime.

description: I'd like to request admin access to the marketing shared drive for a new starter joining next month.
reasoning: A routine, scheduled request with no urgency and no current blocker.

description: Smoke is coming out of the back of the server rack in the IT closet.
reasoning: A literal safety issue (fire risk) -- the clearest possible Critical case.

description: The online learning portal is extremely slow today, pages take 20-30 seconds to load.
reasoning: A widely-used system degraded for everyone, with no real alternative -- important work (coursework access) cannot continue normally, but it's degraded rather than fully down.

description: My keyboard is missing the 'E' key cap, it fell off, but the key still types fine if I press the stem.
reasoning: Cosmetic/minor annoyance; the keyboard is still fully functional.

description: I can't find the setting to change my display language in the student portal, can someone point me to it?
reasoning: A how-to question rather than a fault with hardware, software or network, and nothing is actually broken.

description: The office WiFi has completely vanished from the list of available networks on every device, not just mine.
reasoning: A serious issue significantly affecting work with no reasonable workaround stated -- ticketPrompt.js's own High definition.

description: Video calls keep freezing for everyone on our team during client meetings, happened twice this morning already.
reasoning: Significantly affects work for a team with no workaround offered -- client-facing, no reasonable alternative stated.

description: I can't print over the network from my desk, but I can save the file to a USB stick and print from another computer down the hall.
reasoning: Minor impact with a clearly available workaround -- the prompt's own Low definition, almost verbatim.

description: Quick question -- what's the policy on using a personal phone for two-factor authentication?
reasoning: A policy question, not a fault; nothing is broken and nothing is urgent.

description: Could someone point me to the IT training videos for new starters? No rush, just getting settled in.
reasoning: Explicitly "no rush"; a simple request with no technical problem behind it.

description: None of the laptops in the training room will turn on and a certification exam starts in 20 minutes.
reasoning: Serious, time-critical, no workaround -- but scoped to one room's equipment, not an essential system down for a large group/org, so High rather than Critical.

description: The license for our design software expired overnight and nobody on the team can open their project files until it's renewed.
reasoning: Blocks a whole team from their work with no reasonable workaround -- a licensing problem, not an outage affecting a large group/org, so High.

description: My work email is completely locked and I can't reach anyone for help -- I have a client proposal due today.
reasoning: Total lockout from a core system with real business impact today and no stated alternative -- not an org-wide outage, so High.

description: The clock on the breakroom microwave is showing the wrong time. Not a big deal, just noticed it.
reasoning: Explicitly minor ("not a big deal"), cosmetic, and doesn't affect anyone's actual work.

description: My desktop wallpaper keeps resetting to the default company image every time I log back in.
reasoning: Cosmetic annoyance with zero effect on the ability to do any actual work.

description: Could I get the newer version of Slack installed sometime? Whenever's convenient, no particular hurry.
reasoning: Explicitly no hurry; a simple request rather than something broken.

description: The payroll system is completely down for the entire finance team, and the pay run deadline is this afternoon.
reasoning: An essential system unavailable to a whole team with a hard same-day deadline -- squarely the prompt's own Critical definition.

description: I'm getting sign-in alerts for my account from a country I've never been to -- I think someone's trying to get in.
reasoning: A live, serious security incident -- Critical regardless of how many people are affected so far.

description: The badge reader at the staff entrance has stopped recognising any cards and people are stuck outside in the rain.
reasoning: A genuine safety issue (people stuck outside in weather) plus an essential access system down for everyone -- Critical.

description: The shared printer on my floor isn't working, but I can email the file to a colleague nearby and have them print it for me.
reasoning: Minor impact with an available workaround already in use -- Low.

description: The WiFi signal in meeting room 4B is weak and my calls drop in there, but it works fine at my desk so I have been taking calls from there instead.
reasoning: One room, one person, and a working alternative (the desk) -- minor impact with a workaround, so Low.

description: Since yesterday's update Teams notifications no longer pop up on my laptop, so I keep missing messages unless I open the app and check it myself.
reasoning: Affects one person and work continues only partly (messages are missed) -- a normal individual issue, Medium.

description: I can log in to the staff portal but the timesheet page says I do not have permission, so I cannot submit my hours, which are due on Friday.
reasoning: A permission problem for one person with a deadline days away, not hours -- Medium, not High.

description: The IT service desk phone line plays the office-closed message even during business hours. Emailing the desk still works.
reasoning: Not a device, app, network or account fault, so Other. Email is a working alternative -- Low.

description: The student enrolment system is down for everyone and today is the last day students can enrol.
reasoning: An essential system unavailable to a whole organisation on its deadline day -- Critical.
